text_en: When Nicanor heard that Judas and his troops were in the region of Samaria, he made plans to attack them with complete safety on the day of rest.
text_cn: 尼加诺尔听说犹大和他的部下都在撒玛黎雅附近，便决意要在安息日那天攻击他们，可确保胜利；

text_en: When the Jews who were compelled to follow him said, “Do not destroy so savagely and barbarously, but show respect for the day that he who sees all things has honored and hallowed above other days, ”
text_cn: 但那些被迫跟随他的犹太人却反对说：“你切不要这样残忍凶悍地去屠杀人，应当尊敬观察万物者所圣化的日子！”

text_en: the thrice-accursed wretch asked if there were a sovereign in heaven who had commanded the keeping of the sabbath day.
text_cn: 那罪大恶极的人问道：“天上是否有位命令守安息日的主宰？”

text_en: When they declared, “It is the living Lord himself, the Sovereign in heaven, who ordered us to observe the seventh day, ”
text_cn: 他们率直地答说：“有一位永生的天主，是天上的主宰，他命令守安息日。”

text_en: he replied, “But I am a sovereign also, on earth, and I command you to take up arms and finish the king’s business. ” Nevertheless, he did not succeed in carrying out his abominable design.
text_cn: 他答说：“在地上我是主宰。我今命你们拿出武器，执行君王的命令！”虽然如此，他却没有完成那残酷的计谋。

text_en: This Nicanor in his utter boastfulness and arrogance had determined to erect a public monument of victory over Judas and his forces.
text_cn: 可是，尼加诺尔骄傲自大，仍决意要建立一座象征击败犹大和其部下的凯旋坊；

text_en: But Maccabeus did not cease to trust with all confidence that he would get help from the Lord.
text_cn: 玛加伯却时常怀着坚定的信念，全心信赖必得到上主的援助，

text_en: He exhorted his troops not to fear the attack of the Gentiles, but to keep in mind the former times when help had come to them from heaven, and so to look for the victory that the Almighty would give them.
text_cn: 劝勉自己的同志，不必害怕外邦人的攻击，只该怀念昔日从天上赐予他们的援助，深信此时全能者也必赐给他们胜利。

text_en: Encouraging them from the law and the prophets, and reminding them also of the struggles they had won, he made them the more eager.
text_cn: 后又用法律和先知的话来鼓励他们，又叫他们回忆所经历的战争，使他们都热情勃发。

text_en: When he had aroused their courage, he issued his orders, at the same time pointing out the perfidy of the Gentiles and their violation of oaths.
text_cn: 激起他们作战的精神以后，又宣示外邦人如何失信，违犯誓言， 遂发出攻击的命令。

text_en: He armed each of them not so much with confidence in shields and spears as with the inspiration of brave words, and he cheered them all by relating a dream, a sort of vision, which was worthy of belief.
text_cn: 他武装每个兵士，并不靠盾牌和长枪，而是用极富鼓励的话向他们讲述了一个很可信梦， ──即一个异像──使他们非常高兴。

text_en: What he saw was this: Onias, who had been high priest, a noble and good man, of modest bearing and gentle manner, one who spoke fittingly and had been trained from childhood in all that belongs to excellence, was praying with outstretched hands for the whole body of the Jews.
text_cn: 他所见的异像是这样：他看见一个人，举起双手为整个犹太民族祈祷。这人就是为人善良敦厚，待人谦和，态度温雅，善于辞令，自幼勤修各样德行的前任大司祭敖尼雅。

text_en: Then in the same fashion another appeared, distinguished by his gray hair and dignity, and of marvelous majesty and authority.
text_cn: 接着，又看见一人显现，同样为犹太民族祈祷。他头发苍白，体面端雅，尊严非凡，令人起敬。

text_en: And Onias spoke, saying, “This is a man who loves the family of Israel and prays much for the people and the holy city—Jeremiah, the prophet of God. ”
text_cn: 敖尼雅便解释说：“这是爱护弟兄的人，他就是常为百姓及圣城祈祷的，天主的先知耶肋米亚。”

text_en: Jeremiah stretched out his right hand and gave to Judas a golden sword, and as he gave it he addressed him thus:
text_cn: 随后，耶肋米亚伸出右手，交给犹大一把金剑说：

text_en: “Take this holy sword, a gift from God, with which you will strike down your adversaries. ”
text_cn: “你收下这把圣剑！这是天主的恩赐，你要用来击杀敌人。”

text_en: Encouraged by the words of Judas, so noble and so effective in arousing valor and awaking courage in the souls of the young, they determined not to carry on a campaign but to attack bravely, and to decide the matter by fighting hand to hand with all courage, because the city and the sanctuary and the temple were in danger.
text_cn: 听到了犹大这番美妙言辞的鼓励，人心大为振作，青年的斗志因而坚强起来，因此大家决定不再留守营中，要奋勇进攻拚命与敌人决战，因为京城、宗教与圣殿，都陷在危险中。

text_en: Their concern for wives and children, and also for brothers and sisters and relatives, lay upon them less heavily; their greatest and first fear was for the consecrated sanctuary.
text_cn: 他们对妻子、儿女、兄弟及亲友并不怎么挂虑，最挂虑的却是神圣的圣殿。

text_en: And those who had to remain in the city were in no little distress, being anxious over the encounter in the open country.
text_cn: 留在城中的人也非常焦虑，为那些在外作战的人放心不下。

text_en: When all were now looking forward to the coming issue, and the enemy was already close at hand with their army drawn up for battle, the elephants strategically stationed and the cavalry deployed on the flanks,
text_cn: 众人都期待着快要来临的决战。那时，敌人都已聚集严阵以待，象队已摆在重要的据点，马队已分成左右两翼。

text_en: Maccabeus, observing the masses that were in front of him and the varied supply of arms and the savagery of the elephants, stretched out his hands toward heaven and called upon the Lord who works wonders; for he knew that it is not by arms, but as the Lord decides, that he gains the victory for those who deserve it.
text_cn: 玛加伯见配备各样武器的大军，及凶猛的象队已摆好阵势，便举手向天，呼求施行奇迹的上主；他知道胜利并不在乎武器，而在于上主断定谁应胜利，就使谁胜利。

text_en: He called upon him in these words: “O Lord, you sent your angel in the time of King Hezekiah of Judea, and he killed fully one hundred eighty-five thousand in the camp of Sennacherib.
text_cn: 犹大又祈祷说：“无上的主宰！在犹大王希则克雅时，你曾派遣你的天使，斩杀了散乃黑黎布的军队约十八万五千人。

text_en: So now, O Sovereign of the heavens, send a good angel to spread terror and trembling before us.
text_cn: 上天的主宰，求你现在也派遣一位好天使来，在我们前散布恐怖惊惶。

text_en: By the might of your arm may these blasphemers who come against your holy people be struck down. ” With these words he ended his prayer.
text_cn: 求你用你大能的手，打击这些谩骂和攻击你圣民的人！”他就这样结束了祈祷。

text_en: Nicanor and his troops advanced with trumpets and battle songs,
text_cn: 那时，尼加诺尔率领军队，吹着号角，唱着军歌，蜂拥而来。

text_en: but Judas and his troops met the enemy in battle with invocations to God and prayers.
text_cn: 犹大的部下却在哀求与祈祷声中，前去迎敌，

text_en: So, fighting with their hands and praying to God in their hearts, they laid low at least thirty-five thousand, and were greatly gladdened by God’s manifestation.
text_cn: 徒手作战，心中不住呼求天主，因此击杀了不下三万五千人，万分高兴天主明显的助佑。

text_en: When the action was over and they were returning with joy, they recognized Nicanor, lying dead, in full armor.
text_cn: 战后，他们兴高彩烈回来时，发觉尼加诺尔穿着全副武装，卧地阵亡，

text_en: Then there was shouting and tumult, and they blessed the Sovereign Lord in the language of their ancestors.
text_cn: 一时高声欢呼，用本国语言称颂无上的主宰。

text_en: Then the man who was ever in body and soul the defender of his people, the man who maintained his youthful goodwill toward his compatriots, ordered them to cut off Nicanor’s head and arm and carry them to Jerusalem.
text_cn: 那位完全奉献身心为同胞奋斗，一生热爱民族的犹大，便命人将尼加诺尔的头和手臂砍下，带到耶路撒冷去。

text_en: When he arrived there and had called his compatriots together and stationed the priests before the altar, he sent for those who were in the citadel.
text_cn: 他一到那里，便召集同胞和司祭，又派人将堡垒里的人召来；然后站在祭坛前，

text_en: He showed them the vile Nicanor’s head and that profane man’s arm, which had been boastfully stretched out against the holy house of the Almighty.
text_cn: 将这可恶的尼加诺尔的头，并将他为亵渎谩骂全能者圣殿而举过的手，出示给众人看。

text_en: He cut out the tongue of the ungodly Nicanor and said that he would feed it piecemeal to the birds and would hang up these rewards of his folly opposite the sanctuary.
text_cn: 然后，又割下这邪恶尼加诺尔的舌头，下令切成碎块，以饲飞鸟，并将这狂妄的手臂，挂在圣殿前面。

text_en: And they all, looking to heaven, blessed the Lord who had manifested himself, saying, “Blessed is he who has kept his own place undefiled! ”
text_cn: 那时众人都向天赞颂荣耀的上主说：“那位保卫圣所不受玷污的，应受赞美！”

text_en: Judas hung Nicanor’s head from the citadel, a clear and conspicuous sign to everyone of the help of the Lord.
text_cn: 犹大又将尼加诺尔的头，悬在堡垒上，作为上主援助极显明昭著的记号。

text_en: And they all decreed by public vote never to let this day go unobserved, but to celebrate the thirteenth day of the twelfth month—which is called Adar in the Aramaic language—the day before Mordecai’s day.
text_cn: 众人一致决议，不可让这一天平淡地过去，而该在每年十二月，叙利亚语名“阿达尔”月，十三日，即摩尔德开节前日，隆重庆祝。

text_en: This, then, is how matters turned out with Nicanor, and from that time the city has been in the possession of the Hebrews. So I will here end my story.
text_cn: 这就是有关尼加诺尔的事。从此以后，京城便由希伯来人占领。我也就此结束此记述。

text_en: If it is well told and to the point, that is what I myself desired; if it is poorly done and mediocre, that was the best I could do.
text_cn: 此书若叙述得体，编辑完善，这才是我的愿望；若嫌写得肤浅平凡，但我已尽了我之所能。

text_en: For just as it is harmful to drink wine alone, or, again, to drink water alone, while wine mixed with water is sweet and delicious and enhances one’s enjoyment, so also the style of the story delights the ears of those who read the work. And here will be the end.
text_cn: 比方人只喝酒，或只喝水，都不免有害；但酒水调和了再喝，才有滋味，畅快人心；同样，若史事编纂的巧妙，读此史事的人，才感兴趣。──全书终。
